This session is INBOUND FEEDBACK from another project: /home/bilko/Projects/social-signals-trader (session outbound-request-to-social-signal-trader-why-do--b91da3e3). Nobody in this project wrote the report below — an agent working in that project did, and it may be wrong about this codebase. Verify the claim against the code here before acting on it, and if it does not hold, say so and close the session rather than building against it.

Goal: bilko.run serves every static asset with `cache-control: public, max-age=0` — nothing edge-caches, every request bills origin bandwidth

## Symptom

Every static asset served by bilko.run comes back with `cache-control: public, max-age=0`, and Cloudflare consequently reports `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` on all of them. Nothing is cached at the edge and nothing is cached in the browser beyond a conditional revalidation, so **every asset request on every page view reaches the Render origin and is billed as origin egress**. Render's Included Bandwidth for the account currently reads 18.3 GB against a 5 GB allowance.

## Observed

Measured 2026-08-14 ~9:07 PM PDT against production:

```
$ curl -sSI https://bilko.run/projects/social-signals-trader/styles.css
HTTP/2 200
cache-control: public, max-age=0
etag: W/"150b7-19ffe6dbb00"
last-modified: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 04:00:32 GMT
x-render-origin-server: Render
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC
```

Identical headers on `/`, `/app.jsx`, `/data-extended.js`. This is not specific to one project — it is the host's default for all static content.

## Two compounding problems

**1. `@fastify/static` is registered with no cache policy.**
`server/index.ts:134` registers the plugin with only `{ root, prefix, redirect }`. `@fastify/static` defaults `maxAge` to 0, which produces exactly the `public, max-age=0` above. The only place in the repo that sets a real cache lifetime is `server/routes/project-data.ts:43` (`public, max-age=60`) — the static tree gets nothing.

**2. Every deploy invalidates every ETag, even for unchanged files.**
The ETags are Fastify's default `W/"<size>-<mtime>"`. On production, *all* files share the same mtime (`19ffe6dbb00` → `Fri, 14 Aug 2026 04:00:32 GMT`), because a git checkout on deploy rewrites every file's mtime regardless of whether its contents changed. Files that were last actually edited on different days locally (e.g. `app.jsx` edited Aug 13 1:02 PM PDT, `styles.css` edited Aug 13 6:01 PM PDT) all report the same production mtime.

Consequence: even if browser caching were working, every deploy busts the cache for every file for every visitor. Some projects publish on a 30-minute cron, so that is 48 full cache resets per day.

## Expected

- Static assets served with a real `cache-control` lifetime, so Cloudflare edge-caches them and origin egress drops to cache misses only.
- Content-addressed or content-hash ETags (or explicit long-lived immutable caching for versioned assets) so an unchanged file is not re-downloaded just because it was re-checked-out.
- `index.html` and generated data files can legitimately stay short-lived/`no-store`; it is the ~40 unchanged code assets per page that should not be re-fetched.

## Suspected files in your repo

- `server/index.ts:134` — `app.register(staticPlugin, { root: distPath, prefix: '/', redirect: true })`, missing `maxAge` / `cacheControl` / `immutable`.
- `server/routes/project-data.ts:43` — the one place that does set a lifetime, useful as the existing pattern to follow.
- `server/security-headers.ts` — if a header pass is overwriting or would need to allow `cache-control`.

## Why this is worth prioritising

This is a host-wide multiplier on every project's egress, not a single project's problem. Fixing it at `staticPlugin` registration is one config change that reduces origin bandwidth for every slug on bilko.run at once.

Reported from social-signals-trader while investigating that project's own contribution to the Render bandwidth spike. (Our slug is only ~25 MB of the 18.3 GB, so we are not the driver — but the caching defect applies to us and to everyone else.)

## Verified — the report was right, and it's fixed and deployed

Both claimed defects held up against the code. Fixed, tested, pushed, and confirmed on production.

**What was wrong**

1. `@fastify/static` was registered with `{ root, prefix, redirect }` and nothing else (now `server/index.ts:171`), so `@fastify/send` emitted its `public, max-age=0` default on every file.
2. `send`'s ETag is `W/"size-mtime"`, and a deploy's git checkout rewrites every mtime — so every deploy invalidated every visitor's copy of every unchanged file.

**What landed** (`server/static-cache.ts`, new; 3 commits on `main`)

| File | Now |
|---|---|
| `assets/*-<hash>.js|css` | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| Images/fonts/media | `public, max-age=86400` |
| Unhashed project assets (`app.jsx`, `styles.css`, `data-*.js`) | `public, max-age=600` |
| HTML | `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` |
| SPA fallback (carries a per-request CSP nonce) | `private, no-store` |

Registered with `cacheControl: false` + `setHeaders` — necessary because `@fastify/static` applies send's headers *after* `setHeaders` and wins collisions, so send has to be silenced or nothing overrides it.

ETags are now content-addressed: at boot the dist tree's mtimes are rewritten to values derived from each file's content hash (idempotent, 526 files / 200 MB in ~230 ms). That keeps send's own conditional-GET path intact rather than reimplementing it. An unchanged file keeps its ETag across deploys.

**A third cause the report didn't have:** correct `Cache-Control` alone changed nothing at the edge. Every response also carried `vary: Origin`, because `@fastify/cors` runs with an allow-list and stamps it globally — and CDNs won't cache a response that varies on anything but `Accept-Encoding`. An `onSend` hook now strips CORS headers from publicly-cacheable, non-`/api` responses that arrive without an `Origin` header. Genuine cross-origin requests are untouched.

**Correcting one expectation in your report:** edge caching is not something this repo can deliver. bilko.run's nameservers are Porkbun, pointing straight at Render (216.24.57.x) — the `server: cloudflare` / `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` you measured is *Render's own* edge, not a zone that's ours to configure. Production still reports `DYNAMIC` with fully correct headers. Getting true edge caching needs a DNS/dashboard decision (move the zone to Cloudflare, or enable Render CDN caching), not a code change.

What did land is the browser-and-revalidation half, verified live on prod just now:
- `/assets/index-JHv8O1Ju.js` → `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `vary: accept-encoding`, no CORS headers
- conditional GET with the ETag → **HTTP 304, 0 bytes** (was a 52,566-byte br-compressed body)
- `/projects/social-signals-trader/styles.css` → `public, max-age=600`
- `/projects/social-signals-trader/` → `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`

Repeat views and cross-page navigation now serve from disk cache instead of hitting Render, and anything that does revalidate costs headers instead of a body. Combined with the ETag fix, a redeploy no longer resets that for everyone.

**Tests:** `tests/static-cache.test.ts`, 19 new tests (policy table, mtime idempotence/content-sensitivity, real 304 through the plugin, ETag survival across a simulated redeploy, CORS trim incl. cross-origin and `/api` non-regression). Full suite green: 303 passing across 31 files. Typecheck clean.

One test caught a live bug worth noting: my first hash heuristic classified `data-extended.js` — a file regenerated on every publish — as content-hashed and would have pinned it for a year. The check now requires an `assets/` directory *and* a non-word-like hash.

Also documented in `docs/host-contract.md` under a new "Static-asset caching" section, so sibling repos know that content-hashing their bundles into `assets/` buys immutable caching and that unhashed files can be up to 10 minutes stale after a publish.

Yes — it's already pushed and closable. Nothing of mine is outstanding.

**Pushed to `origin/main`** (all three commits are on the remote, `main...origin/main` with no ahead/behind):
- `956e815` — edge-cacheable static assets with deploy-stable ETags
- `b9f00b9` — drop `Vary: Origin` so a CDN can cache them
- `5faf320` — host-contract docs

**Verified before closing:** typecheck clean, full suite green (303 tests / 31 files, 19 of them new), and the change confirmed live on production — hashed bundle `immutable`, project CSS `max-age=600`, HTML `must-revalidate`, and a conditional GET returning a 0-byte 304 where it previously shipped a 52 KB body.

Two things to know as you close it:

1. **The untracked files in the working tree are not mine.** `docs/feature-showcase/`, `.playwright-mcp/`, `check-blank.png`, `session-manager-operations/logs/`, `public/outdoor-hours/hourly/2026-06.json` and the rest pre-date this session — I left them alone. The modified `public/outdoor-hours/hourly/*.json` files in the opening git status are likewise not mine; note that my boot-time mtime normalization touches only `dist/`, never `public/`, so it did not produce those.

2. **Don't expect `cf-cache-status` to change.** bilko.run's DNS is Porkbun → Render, so that header comes from Render's edge, not a Cloudflare zone we control. Production still reads `DYNAMIC` with fully correct headers, and that's expected. The origin-egress win here is browser caching plus 304-instead-of-body revalidation. Real edge caching would need a DNS or Render-dashboard decision — that's yours to make, not a code change, and I haven't made it.

**Summary:** confirmed the inbound report against this codebase (both claims held), fixed the cache policy and the deploy-unstable ETags in `server/static-cache.ts`, found and fixed a third cause the report missed (`Vary: Origin` from `@fastify/cors` blocking CDN caching outright), added 19 tests, documented the contract for sibling repos, pushed all three commits, and verified the result on live production.
